description:
## Context

Phone-agent needs two interrelated contracts before the greenfield scenario can be built: a routine model (recurring or ad-hoc agent calls registered against the system) and an agent-manager runner contract (how each voice turn maps to an agent-manager run). These are coupled — the routine model depends on what the runner can express per turn — so they are researched together.

## Research Goals

### 1. Routine model
- What is a routine? Candidate fields: skill id, context-prep source (e.g., a file path or upstream agent output), agent-manager profile, schedule, transport preferences, retry policy
- How routines are registered, stored, and discovered
- How scheduled triggers fire and dispatch outbound calls
- Relationship to the existing director-swarm vision-walk-prep agent (does its last-handoff.md become pre-turn context for the morning-vision-walk routine? does the prep agent become a routine pre-hook?)
- Inbound caller-ID to routine resolution

### 2. Agent-manager runner contract
- One agent-manager run per user utterance (multi-phase runs / sessions are P2 in agent-manager — OT-P2-001 — so phone-agent owns conversation history)
- Conversation history packing strategy for each per-turn run
- Token-level assistant deltas in the agent-manager event stream — required so phone-agent can start TTS on the first sentence without waiting for the full response. Confirm whether agent-manager already exposes this; if not, file a follow-up fix after this research concludes.
- Agent-manager profile constraints per routine (read-only for discussion phases, write-enabled for action phases like creating backlog items)
- Sandbox / acceptance_allow strategy per routine (most routines should not modify code)

## Deliverables

- Routine schema + dispatch model
- Per-turn run shape (input format, history packing, event handling)
- Token-streaming gap analysis with a follow-up fix item if a gap exists
- Profile/policy guidance for read-only vs write-enabled routines
